intent: A persistent row of application menus, such as File, Edit and View, that moves focus between their triggers with the arrow keys and switches between the menus while one is open.
typical_uses: The command bar across the top of an application or a document editor

dont_use_when.situation: One menu of actions on its own, with no sibling menus beside it
Site or application navigation between pages
A row of buttons that each run an action directly, with no menu behind them
A menu opened by right-clicking or long-pressing an area

invariants.text: The bar renders `role="menubar"` with `aria-orientation` and holds one tab stop; the arrow keys along its `orientation` move focus between its MenubarTriggers, Home and End move to the first and the last, and focus wraps at the ends unless `loopFocus` is false.
While one of its menus is open, moving to another MenubarTrigger of the bar, by arrow key or by hovering it, opens that trigger's menu and closes the first, with no click.

While a menu of a modal bar (`modal`, true when not given) is open, page scroll is locked and pointer interaction outside the bar and the open popup is blocked, while the bar itself stays usable so the pointer can move to a sibling trigger; with `modal={false}` the rest of the page stays usable.
Setting `disabled` on the bar disables every MenubarTrigger in it and every MenubarMenu it holds.

menubar.module.css lays the triggers out in a row whatever the `orientation`; `orientation` sets `aria-orientation` and which arrow keys move between the triggers, and the menus still open below their triggers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the menubar's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the menubar's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (orientation, modal, hasSubmenuOpen). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through menubar.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A File and a View menu in one bar
good.code:
<Menubar>
  <MenubarMenu>
    <MenubarTrigger>File</MenubarTrigger>
    <MenubarContent>
      <MenubarItem>
        New tab
        <MenubarShortcut>⌘T</MenubarShortcut>
      </MenubarItem>
      <MenubarSeparator />
      <MenubarItem variant="destructive">Close window</MenubarItem>
    </MenubarContent>
  </MenubarMenu>
  <MenubarMenu>
    <MenubarTrigger>View</MenubarTrigger>
    <MenubarContent>
      <MenubarCheckboxItem checked={showBookmarks} onCheckedChange={setShowBookmarks}>
        Show bookmarks
      </MenubarCheckboxItem>
    </MenubarContent>
  </MenubarMenu>
</Menubar>

bad.title: DropdownMenu parts assembled into a bar
bad.why: The bar accepts MenubarMenu; a DropdownMenuTrigger has no styling of its own, so it draws as a bare button in the bar, and its popup keeps the standalone placement instead of the bar's.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, MenubarState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the menubar's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through menubar.module.css, not through this.
